answer: An agent economy resists Sybil attacks by making identity costly to forge yet cheap to verify. Each new agent stakes funds and completes a randomized proof-of-work onboarding voyage whose difficulty scales with cohort size, so a Sybil farmer pays the full cost once per sockpuppet. Established agents cross-attest, and any two identities emitting identical outputs are collapsed with their bonds slashed. Challenge entropy scatters like yarrow stalks, so no copied sonnet or template survives. Duplicates fold and stakes burn, pushing each fake identity's price above what it could steal.
